procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine BP visit. Turned 50 last month.
No new symptoms. Home readings low 130s/80s. Takes HCTZ in the morning with coffee.
Sober four years this month.
Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs clear. RRR. Abdomen benign. No edema.
A/P: HTN stable, continue HCTZ 25. LFTs and BMP today. Physical in June; Shingrix and PCV20 then, and she's due for a Pap.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: eRx renewal request, HCTZ 25 mg daily #90. Seen 2/21, BMP normal. Sent with 3 refills.

reports.text: Specimen: ThinPrep, cervical/endocervical. Adequacy: satisfactory, transformation zone component present. High-risk HPV: not detected.
reports.conclusion: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. HPV negative.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Moved up from September so we could fold in the Pap and the 50+ vaccines.

Feels well. No headaches, palpitations or sweats. No alcohol. Working hybrid.

Exam: well appearing. Anicteric. Thyroid normal. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Breasts without mass, skin change or nipple discharge; axillae negative. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly, no fluid. Pelvic: external genitalia normal, cervix without lesion, Pap/HPV collected; bimanual normal. Skin without rash. No edema.

A/P
- Prevention: Pap with HPV. Shingrix #1 and PCV20 today (chronic liver disease, prior heavy alcohol use). Shingrix #2 in 2 months. Mammogram due late fall. Colonoscopy current.
- HTN: well controlled.
- Hep C: CMP, CBC.
- Lipids today.

documents.title: Pap and labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Julie, good news all around. Your Pap is normal and HPV testing is negative, so the next one isn't due for five years. Bloodwork is your usual pattern: liver enzymes a bit high, everything else normal. Cholesterol fine. Shingrix #2 any time after August 20.

documents.title: RE: Pap and labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you! Booked the second shot for the 22nd. The first one gave me chills for a night, is that normal?

documents.title: RE: Pap and labs
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Yes, a night of chills or achiness is common with Shingrix and it can happen again with the second dose. Acetaminophen is fine at regular doses. See you on the 22nd.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Shingrix #2 given L deltoid. Series complete. Reminded her the arm may be sore for a couple of days.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu (R arm) and bivalent Pfizer booster (L arm) at the evening clinic. Screening negative. Waited 15 minutes, no reaction.

events.reason: Episodes of headache, racing heart and sweating

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: Paroxysmal headache, palpitations, diaphoresis with hypertension

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: spells.

HPI: Since around July she has had episodes, at first maybe twice a month and now most weeks: pounding headache, heart racing, drenched in sweat, lasting 10 to 30 minutes. Several came while carrying boxes up the stairs at work or rushing; a couple during a stressful meeting. During the worst ones she has a feeling that something terrible is about to happen. Her home cuff read very high during one episode, and between episodes it has been running above her usual. No chest pain, no syncope, no weight change, no tremor, no new medicines or supplements, no decongestants, no caffeine change. No alcohol.

Exam: BP high as charted, recheck similar. Appears well between episodes. No thyromegaly. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no bruit, no mass. Skin warm.

A/P
Paroxysmal headache, palpitations, diaphoresis with newly uncontrolled HTN. Pheochromocytoma has to be excluded first; also thyroid. Plasma free metanephrines and normetanephrines (drawn seated, she's not on anything that interferes), TSH, BMP.
HCTZ unchanged for now. Asked her to keep a log of episodes and home BP. Will call with results. ED for chest pain or a headache that doesn't settle.

orders.order: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
orders.reason: Elevated plasma metanephrines, localize adrenal source

documents.title: Results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt. Plasma free metanephrine 480 and normetanephrine 1,350 pg/mL, both well above the lab's upper limits; TSH normal. Glucose 110, K 3.5, creatinine 0.9. Explained that this pattern points to a catecholamine-producing tumor, most often in the adrenal gland, and that it's treatable. Ordering CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast to look at the adrenals. She'll avoid heavy lifting at work until we know more. Endocrinology referral once imaging is back. She'll call back if more questions come up.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
Technique: helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis after IV contrast, portal venous phase, with delayed adrenal images.
Adrenals: 3.0 cm heterogeneous, avidly enhancing left adrenal mass without macroscopic fat; attenuation and enhancement are not those of a lipid-rich adenoma. Right adrenal normal.
Liver normal in size and contour without focal lesion. Gallbladder surgically absent; no biliary dilation. Spleen, pancreas and kidneys normal. No lymphadenopathy. No ascites. Bowel, bladder, uterus and ovaries unremarkable. Bones unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: 3 cm left adrenal mass with features suggesting pheochromocytoma in the setting of elevated metanephrines. No other abnormality.

orders.reason: Left adrenal mass with elevated plasma metanephrines, probable pheochromocytoma

documents.title: CT result, referral
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed CT with pt by phone: 3 cm left adrenal mass that looks like a pheochromocytoma, nothing else found. Urgent endocrine referral placed; spoke with their triage nurse, first opening Jan 2. Precautions until then: no decongestants, no heavy exertion, call or go to the ED for a spell that won't stop, chest pain or severe headache. Continue HCTZ. She was relieved to have an answer.

reports.text: Bilateral screening tomosynthesis mammogram. Prior studies 2019-2021 reviewed. Scattered fibroglandular density. Stable right intramammary node. No suspicious mass, calcifications or distortion.

documents.title: Mammogram result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Benign. Letter sent.

conditions.label: Benign neoplasm of left adrenal gland

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group
Date of visit: 01/02/2023
Re: Julie Lambert, DOB 01/27/1972

Dear Doctor,
Thank you for asking us to see Ms. Lambert, 50, for spells and a left adrenal mass.

For roughly half a year she has had attacks of headache, palpitations and sweating, sometimes with a feeling of impending doom, often brought on by exertion or stress. Background: chronic hepatitis C genotype 1a since 2011 with an unfinished antiviral course, hypertension on hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, alcohol use disorder in remission since 2018, cholecystectomy 2014. NKDA. Never smoker. Mother with hypertension and breast cancer; father with alcohol-related cirrhosis; maternal aunt with lung cancer; brother with type 2 diabetes. She works as an office administrator.

Exam: BP 170/95 in clinic. Well nourished, mildly distressed. Skin notably moist. No abdominal bruit or palpable mass.

Data: your labs (glucose 110 mg/dL, potassium 3.5, creatinine 0.9; plasma free metanephrines elevated) and CT (3 cm left adrenal mass, features of pheochromocytoma). We added a 24-hour urine collection, completed 01/05: urinary metanephrines and normetanephrines both elevated.

Impression: pheochromocytoma, left adrenal, biochemically and radiographically confirmed.

Plan:
1. Surgical resection: referred to endocrine surgery for laparoscopic left adrenalectomy.
2. Alpha blockade: doxazosin 2 mg daily started, liberal salt and fluids, home BP twice daily. We will adjust before surgery.
3. Continue HCTZ for now.
4. Postoperative plasma metanephrines 6-8 weeks after surgery, then yearly.

Sincerely,
Endocrinology

documents.title: Surgery date
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI the surgeon's office called, adrenal surgery is Feb 22. Do you need to do anything before? Also the doxazosin is fine, BP at home mostly 130s now.

documents.title: RE: Surgery date
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know. Their team handles the pre-op workup and labs; if they ask for a clearance letter from us, just have them fax the form. Glad the numbers are better. Keep taking the doxazosin exactly as endocrinology told you.

conditions.label: Benign neoplasm of left adrenal gland

reports.text:
Specimen: left adrenal gland, laparoscopic adrenalectomy.
Gross: adrenal gland 28 g containing a well-circumscribed tan-red mass, 3.0 x 2.7 x 2.5 cm.
Microscopic: nested (zellballen) chromaffin cell neoplasm, chromogranin and synaptophysin positive, with S100-positive sustentacular cells. Tumor confined to the adrenal gland. Margins negative. No lymphovascular invasion identified.
reports.conclusion: Pheochromocytoma, 3.0 cm, confined to the adrenal gland; margins negative.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Endocrine Surgery
documents.author: endocrine surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital, endocrine surgery service
Admitted 02/22/2023, discharged 02/24/2023

Procedure: laparoscopic left adrenalectomy, 02/22/2023.
Indication: left adrenal pheochromocytoma. Preoperative alpha blockade with doxazosin per endocrinology.
Course: uncomplicated. Ambulating and tolerating a regular diet by postoperative day 1.
Pathology: pheochromocytoma, 3.0 cm, margins negative.
Discharge medications: stop doxazosin. Continue hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. Acetaminophen as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: surgery clinic in 2 weeks; endocrinology for plasma metanephrines in 6-8 weeks; primary care in 1-2 weeks for BP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two weeks out from left adrenalectomy. Pathology was pheo, margins clear.

No spells since surgery. Headaches gone. Port sites a little sore, healing. Off doxazosin per discharge. On HCTZ alone, home BP 120s/70s.

Exam: BP 126/78. Comfortable. Port sites clean, dry, no erythema. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft.

A/P
- S/p left adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma: doing well. Endocrine to check plasma metanephrines in April and yearly after; I'll draw the yearly ones here if they want.
- HTN: back to her old baseline on HCTZ 25. Continue.
Back to work Monday, desk duties; no lifting over 10 lb for 4 weeks per surgery.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group
Visit 04/12/2023

Ms. Lambert returns 7 weeks after laparoscopic left adrenalectomy for a 3.0 cm pheochromocytoma (margins negative). No further paroxysms. BP 124/76 on hydrochlorothiazide alone.

Plasma free metanephrine and normetanephrine today: both normal.

Impression: biochemical cure after resection of pheochromocytoma.
Plan: yearly plasma free metanephrines for at least 10 years; these can be drawn by primary care with results copied to us. Return here sooner for any recurrent spells. Medications unchanged: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. NKDA.

Thank you for allowing us to share in her care.

events.reason: Itchy rash on wrists and ankles

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

orders.reason: Pruritic papular eruption of wrists and ankles with oral involvement

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Itchy bumps started on the inside of both wrists about 6 weeks ago, now on the ankles too, and she has noticed some white patches inside her cheeks. Itching worse at night. No new soaps, detergents, lotions, jewelry or medicines. No fever.

Exam: flat-topped violet papules, a few mm each, on the flexor wrists and both medial ankles. White streaky change on the buccal mucosa. No other rash.

A/P: pruritic papular rash with mouth involvement, looks most like lichen planus, which can go along with hep C. Referred to dermatology to confirm before treating anything; she'd rather wait for them. Cool compresses, fragrance-free moisturizer meanwhile.

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology practice
Date of service: 06/21/2023

Reason for referral: pruritic eruption.

Ms. Lambert has had itchy lesions for about two months, first on the wrists, then the ankles and the inside of the mouth. She has not started any new medication, soap or chemical. History of chronic hepatitis C and a pheochromocytoma resected in February. Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. NKDA.

Examination: purple, flat-topped, angular papules over the flexor wrists and ankles; several show a fine lacy white surface pattern. Lace-like white plaques on the oral mucosa. Fingernails with longitudinal ridges and distal splitting. No lymph nodes enlarged. Remainder of the skin exam unremarkable.

Labs obtained here: CBC normal. AST and ALT mildly elevated. HCV RNA detected. HIV antibody negative.

Assessment: lichen planus, cutaneous, oral and nail, in a patient with active hepatitis C.

Plan: diagnosis discussed. Clobetasol 0.05% ointment, a thin layer twice daily to the itchy skin papules for 2 weeks, then stop. The lacy patches in the mouth are painless and need no treatment; nor do the nails. Return as needed or sooner if the mouth becomes painful.

Dermatology

medications.sig: Apply a thin layer to the itchy skin spots twice daily for 2 weeks, then stop

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: HCTZ 25 mg renewal from pharmacy. BP controlled post-adrenalectomy (3/8, endo 4/12). Sent 90 days x 3. Physical scheduled 9/11.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual.

Year in review: pheo out in February, cured biochemically in April. Lichen planus diagnosed by dermatology in June; still itchy at the wrists some nights, mouth not sore. No spells. Sober 5.5 years.

Meds: HCTZ 25. NKDA.

Exam: well. Faint violet papules on the flexor wrists. Lacy white change in the cheeks, no erosions. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, healed port sites, no organomegaly, no fluid wave. No edema.

A/P
1. Prevention: PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 0. Mammogram due November. Pap 2022 negative, next 2027. Colonoscopy 2021. Shingrix and PCV20 done. Flu and updated COVID next month.
2. HTN: controlled.
3. Hep C: CMP, CBC.
4. Pheo history: plasma metanephrines due February.
5. Lichen planus: per derm.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Julie, labs look like they always do. Liver enzymes mildly high, blood counts, kidney function and cholesterol normal. See you in the winter for the metanephrine check.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: MA
documents.body: 2023-24 Pfizer COVID and flu given, one in each arm. No reactions.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis, compared with 2020-2022. Scattered fibroglandular density. No suspicious findings.

documents.title: Mammogram result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Negative. Annual. Letter.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: Purpura, arthralgia, rising creatinine and active urine sediment with hepatitis C; suspected cryoglobulinemia

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Same-day visit.

Since the weekend: achy pain in both wrists and both knees, same on each side, worse in the morning. Small red-purple spots came up on her shins two days ago. More tired than usual. Pins and needles in her fingers and the soles of her feet on and off. No fever, no sore throat or recent infection, no new medicines. No dark urine she has noticed.

Exam: afebrile. Raised, non-blanching purpuric papules scattered over both lower legs, ankles to mid-shin. Wrists and knees without effusion or warmth, mildly tender. Sensation grossly intact. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

A/P
Palpable purpura, symmetric arthralgia, paresthesias and fatigue in a patient with untreated hepatitis C: mixed cryoglobulinemia until proven otherwise. CMP, CBC and UA now. Urgent nephrology referral regardless of results; if the kidneys are involved they'll want to see her this week. Acetaminophen for joint pain, avoid NSAIDs. Call if the rash spreads, urine darkens, swelling or weakness.

documents.title: Results, nephrology appointment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt. Creatinine 1.2, up from her 0.9 baseline. Urine shows protein and blood. CBC normal, liver enzymes at her usual mild elevation. Called nephrology's on-call line Friday afternoon; they'll see her Monday 1/1 at their urgent session. Pt aware. Rash about the same, joints a bit better with acetaminophen.
